spec.description: Subscribe to client asset balances and account ledger transactions for this account.

users.description: Available on master accounts only. If `all`, events for master and subaccounts are streamed and no snapshot is provided; otherwise only master account events are published.

rebased.description: Effective for viewing xstocks only. If true, display in terms of underlying equity, otherwise in terms of SPV tokens.

anyOf.title: BalancesSnapshotMessage
anyOf.description: Full snapshot of every asset held in the account, sent once right after subscribing.

data.description: One entry per asset held in the account.

items.title: BalanceSnapshotEntry
items.description: An asset's total balance and its per-wallet breakdown, as of the subscription snapshot.

asset_class.description: The asset class -- a placeholder for future expansion.

balance.description: The total amount of asset held across all wallet types.

wallets.description: The per-wallet breakdown of this asset's balance.

items.title: BalanceWallet
items.description: One wallet holding part of an asset's total balance.

balance.description: Balance of the asset in this wallet.

anyOf.title: BalancesUpdateMessage
anyOf.description: One or more account ledger transactions, pushed as each completes.

data.description: One entry per ledger transaction affecting an asset.

items.title: BalanceLedgerEntry
items.description: One account ledger transaction affecting a single asset.

asset_class.description: The asset class -- a placeholder for future expansion.

amount.description: The amount of asset change in this event.

balance.description: The total amount of this asset held in the account after this event.

fee.description: The fee paid on the transaction.

ledger_id.description: The identifier for this account ledger entry.

ref_id.description: A reference identifier in the context of this balance event, e.g. the trade_id for a trade event.

timestamp.description: The time of the balance change. RFC3339, e.g. `2022-12-25T09:30:59.123456Z`.

type.description: The broad type of the balance event.

subtype.description: The specific subtype of the balance event, when applicable.

category.description: The categorization of the balance event.

user.description: The Kraken-generated identifier for a user / sub-account. Only published when the subscription requested `users: "all"`.

notes: Private channel over wss://ws-auth.kraken.com/v2 -- requires a token obtained via REST GetWebSocketsToken. `channel` and `token` are omitted from the subscribe requestBody schema: `channel` is fixed (carried as `spec.channel`) and `token` is injected by the transport (core.md: merged into every outgoing `params` on the private connection), not a caller-supplied parameter -- mirroring how REST private endpoints don't declare `nonce`/`API-Key` in their requestBody either.

`data` genuinely differs in shape between `type: "snapshot"` (BalanceSnapshotEntry, asset totals + per-wallet breakdown) and `type: "update"` (BalanceLedgerEntry, one ledger transaction) -- modeled as a message-level anyOf per authoring rule 4, not one object with every field optional.

`wallets` on BalanceSnapshotEntry is declared required (deviating from the hand-written PoC's `NotRequired[list[Wallet]]` in pkg/src/kraken/streams/private.py): every asset in the documented snapshot example carries it and the docs don't mark it conditional. Worth confirming against a captured example with a zero-wallet asset, if one exists.

`wallet_id`'s enum differs between the snapshot wallet object (adds `flex`, `closed`) and the update ledger entry (`main`, `bonded`, `flexible`, `liquid`, `locked` only) -- kept as two separate enums, each matching exactly what its own doc section lists, rather than merged into one superset.

`fee`, `ledger_id`, `ref_id` on BalanceLedgerEntry are marked required from their presence in both documented update examples (deposit and trade); the docs don't mark any data-item field required or optional explicitly, so this is inferred from examples, not a documented guarantee.

The subscribe reply is split anyOf[BalancesSubscribeAck, BalancesSubscribeError] on `success`, since a failed subscribe carries `error` and no `result` -- same shape as the success/failure reply split rule documented for WS commands.
